title: Thanksgiving Side Dishes
excerpt: Find easy Thanksgiving side dishes for mashed potatoes, stuffing, green beans, and gravy, gathered in one Grandma Recipe guide.
featuredImageAlt: Thanksgiving side dishes with mashed potatoes, stuffing, green beans, and gravy
contentHtml:
The turkey gets the spotlight, but thanksgiving side dishes are what fill the plates. This guide gathers Grandma Recipe’s best holiday sides, from creamy mashed potatoes and rice stuffing to green beans and silky gravy, so you can build a sideboard without last-minute guessing.

Use this page as your sides checklist. Each recipe has clear steps and pantry-friendly ingredients for a full Thanksgiving table, a smaller dinner for two, or make-ahead prep the day before.

How to Use This Thanksgiving Side Dishes Guide

Start with the kind of side you need:

  • Want the classic mash? Open creamy mashed potatoes, loaded mash, or a baked mashed potato casserole.
  • Need something savory beside the bird? Rice stuffing and garlic almond green beans travel well on the plate.
  • Finishing the plate? Homemade gravy (or vegan gravy) ties everything together.
  • Cooking for plant-based guests? Pair vegan mashed potatoes with vegan gravy and rice stuffing.

If you want one first win, start with Creamy Mashed Potatoes. Add Green Beans with Garlic and Almonds and Homemade Gravy, and the sideboard already feels complete. For the full holiday menu, return to Easy Thanksgiving Recipes.

Scroll the potato, stuffing, vegetable, and gravy sections below, then use the simple sideboard checklist when you are ready to shop.

Potato Thanksgiving Sides

Creamy, cozy potato dishes everyone reaches for first.

  • Creamy Mashed Potatoes, fluffy Yukon Gold mashed potatoes with garlic and chives.
  • Ultimate Loaded Mashed Potatoes, loaded mashed potatoes with cheddar, turkey bacon bits, and chives.
  • Mashed Potato Casserole, baked mashed potato casserole with a golden topping.
  • Vegan Mashed Potatoes, creamy dairy-free mashed potatoes for plant-based plates.

Stuffing and Vegetables

Savory stuffing, casseroles, and a fresh green vegetable to balance the richer dishes.

  • Classic Bread Stuffing, classic bread stuffing with onion, celery, and herbs.
  • Rice Stuffing, rice stuffing with onions, celery, cranberries, and herbs.
  • Homestyle Green Bean Casserole, green bean casserole with creamy sauce and crispy onions.
  • Green Beans with Garlic and Almonds, green beans with garlic and toasted almonds.
  • Classic Sweet Potato Casserole, sweet potato casserole with pecan streusel.
  • Homemade Cranberry Sauce, homemade cranberry sauce simmered until glossy.

Gravy for Thanksgiving

Silky gravy for mashed potatoes, stuffing, and turkey.

  • Silky Homemade Turkey Gravy, turkey gravy from drippings or broth, no wine.
  • Homemade Gravy, homemade gravy you can whisk up for the whole table.
  • Vegan Gravy, dairy-free gravy with deep savory flavor.

Build a Simple Sideboard

You do not need eight pans to make Thanksgiving sides feel generous:

  • Pick one potato, creamy mash for tradition or casserole when you want oven-friendly make-ahead.
  • Add one stuffing, rice stuffing is light enough to sit beside turkey without weighing the plate down.
  • Add one green vegetable, garlic almond green beans bring crunch and color.
  • Finish with gravy, warm it last so it stays silky.
  • Serve with turkey and pie, Oven-Roasted Bone Turkey Breast and Classic Homemade Pumpkin Pie complete the classic menu.

FAQs

How many Thanksgiving side dishes do I need?

For most tables, three sides plus gravy is enough: one potato, one stuffing, and one vegetable. Add a second potato dish only if you are feeding a crowd.

Which Thanksgiving side dish should I make first?

Start with Creamy Mashed Potatoes. It is familiar, rewarms well, and pairs with almost every main. Then add Rice Stuffing and Green Beans with Garlic and Almonds.

Can I make Thanksgiving side dishes ahead?

Yes. Rice Stuffing and Mashed Potato Casserole hold well overnight. Mashed potatoes rewarm gently with a splash of milk or broth. Gravy is best finished just before serving.

What are good vegetarian Thanksgiving side dishes?

Build around Vegan Mashed Potatoes, Vegan Gravy, Rice Stuffing, and Green Beans with Garlic and Almonds. Skip turkey bacon toppings on loaded mash if you want a fully meat-free plate.

What gravy goes with mashed potatoes?

Use Homemade Gravy for a classic table, or Vegan Gravy when you need a dairy-free option that still tastes rich.

Final Thoughts

Good thanksgiving side dishes do not need a crowded stove. Choose one potato, one stuffing, one green vegetable, and gravy, then let the oven and a couple of pots do the work. Bookmark this guide, cook what fits your timeline, and come back to Easy Thanksgiving Recipes when you are ready to lock in turkey and dessert.
